User Changed the SOLA Alert Handler

1. The Alert Handler has been updated
2. To complete the process you must cycle power
Error cannot write Stepped Modulation Start Offset
Error cannot write Stepped Modulation Recycle Offset
Delta T Limit has been reached

The Maximum Delta T between the boiler inlet and outlet sensors is exceeded. This indicates low flow.
1) Check the pump and system for proper flow through the boiler.
2)Ensure all water filters and strainers are free of debris.
3) Check the inlet and outlet sensors for proper function.
4) Check the Delta T during operation

The Maximum Outlet Temperature is exceeded.

1. Check settings for operation causing high temperatures.
2. Check applicable pump for proper operation.
3.Check Outlet sensor for proper operation.

The maximum exhaust temperature is exceeded.

1. Check sensor wiring and correct any possible errors.
2.Check for fouled heat exchanger.
3.Check for proper combustion
4.check for proper fan speed
5.Check for proper settings
6. Replace the Stack high limit.
7. If previous steps are correct and fault persists, replace the Sola module.

The communication between the Nuro and the Sola has been lost.

1) Check the wiring connections between the Display Modbus terminals and the Sola MB1 terminals.
2) Check for interferance sources.
3) Check for proper grounding

The inlet sensor temperature is higher than the outlet temperature sensor indicating reverse flow.

1) Check for proper system piping.
2) Check pumping system for proper flow.
The Control program was started at this time.

The Parameter Cascade CH Mode
under the Cascade Master -> General
Settings is set to an invaild selction.

Please Change this value to Setpoint
or None.

The Aux 1 input is selected for more than one function.
Only Normal member boiler start sequence Priority will occur.

Check the Cascade Master Enable and the Cascasde ODA/Aux1 Priority Change parameter. Only one of these parameters should be set to Aux1
ODA sensor Error in Priorty Change

The ODA sensor is Out of Range.
The member boiler start sequence will not be reversed.

Check the ODA sensor and wires.

Check the Cascade ODA/Aux1 Priority Change parameter. Ensure this parameter is set correctly.

The Cascade Member Lost Communication with the Master

Check the Cascade wires between the Master and the Member.

Check that all members have a unique Member address.
The Master has a member number accessed in its member settings.

The Aux 1 input is selected for more than one function.
Aux1 for the Bypass Endswitch will not be used on the Master

Check the Cascade Master Enable and the Cascasde ODA/Aux1 Priority Change parameter. Only one of these may be assigned to use Aux 1.

Aux 1 may be used as the bypass endswitch if the bypass valve is not connected to the master.
No relay is assigned for a bypass valve

The Cascade Master is setup to use a bypass valve. No boiler in the cascade system has a bypass valve selected as a relay assignment.

On the boiler that the bypass valve is connected to, change one of the assigned relays to be a bypass valve.

If a bypass valve is not used then change the Cascade Master - Valve Control -Use Bypass Valve parameter to NO
No relay is assigned for valve control

The cascade Master is set to valve control. You must select a relay output to control a boiler valve.

In the Boiler Settings - Relay Association menu assign a relay to control a Boiler Valve.

One of the Bypass valves failed to make the endswitch in the allowed time.

The system has now opened a boiler valve to maintain flow through the system.

Please verify the bypass valves operation and endswitch connection.

4) Check for the Power LED on the SOLA

High Gas Limit / Dual Fuel Relays

The high gas limit switch has tripped or the Dual Fuel Circuit has detected a problem
1. Check for proper gas valve adjustment.
2. Check for proper gas valve operation.
3. Check fire test valve.
4. Check for proper wiring.
5.Replace switch.
-----------------------------------
1) Check to make sure both Gas Valves do not open simultaneously when the boiler atempts to start.
2) Verify only one Current Switch relay is active at a time when the boiler atempts to start
High Back Pressure in Stack or Burner Hood

One or more High Back Pressure Switches has tripped indicating excessive Flue Back Pressure or High Pressure in the Burner.
1) Check for obstructions in the flue pipe.
2) Check for blocked condensate drain.
3) Check for a blocked heat exchanger.
4) Check for a blocked/ dirty burner.
5 ) Check Operation of the High Back Pressure Switches.
4) Replace the High Back Pressure Switches.
The primary selected Header Sensor failed. Check the sensor.

1. Check wiring and correct any possible errors.
2. Check the Stack Limit Switch. If tripped perform a-d and reset the switch

a.Check for fouled heat exchanger.
b.Check for proper combustion
c.check for proper fan speed
d.Check for proper settings

3. Replace the Stack sensor or Stack Limit Switch.
4. If previous steps are correct and fault persists,
a. Export support files from Nuro to a USB flash drive.
b. Contact Weil-McLain service, they will require these support files..
Burner Door or HX High Temp Fault

The burner door switch or the heat exchanger switch has tripped indicating excessive temperature on the burner door or rear heat exchanger.
1. Determine which switch is tripped.
If either switch is tripped: contact Patterson Kelley factory support.
2.If neither switch is tripped, check the wiring and correct any errors.
3. If previous steps are correct and the fault persists,
a. Export support files from Nuro to a USB flash drive.
b. Contact Weil-McLain service, they will require these support files..

The external Low water level device has tripped indicating insufficient water level in the boiler, or the external jumper is missing

1. Check the external Low Water Sensor (if used) or the terminal strip jumper.
2. Check boiler pump for proper operation.
3. Check the external low water level switch.
4. Check the external low water level probe and connections.

The flow switch opened when it should have been closed.
1. Check the pump
2. Check for flow obstructions

The Fan Speed was not steady during Ignition.
1. Check fan wiring and correct any potential wiring errors.
2. Check that the fan indicates proper RPM.
3. Check ignitor gap.
4. Check proper electrical grounding.
One or All of the Members have Outdated Software. In order to run the Delta T Monitoring the Member software needs to be updated. Please update all the Members to the latest software version.

The Air Inlet Sensor is faulted.
This sensor is connected to the Spare Sensor Input.
The parameter set is configured to use the Spare Sensor as an Air Inlet temperature sensor
1. Check the spare sensor.
2. Check wiring to the spare sensor.
3. Check that parameters are set correctly if no sensor is wired to the spare sensor terminals.

The ODA Sensor is faulted.
The parameter set is configured to use the ODA sensor for freeze protection.
1. Check the outdoor air sensor.
2. Check wiring to the outdoor air sensor.
3. Check that parameters are set correctly.

The Low Air Intake Pressure Switch has tripped indicating excessive negative inlet pressure.
1) Check for obstructions in the air inlet pipe.
2) Check for blocked air inlet
3 ) Check operation of the Low Air Inlet Pressure Switch.
4) Replace the Low Air Inlet Pressure Switch.

A Cascade Member was shutdown due to low flow. The Delta T was higher than allowed.
1) Increase the flow in the system.
2) Check for restrictions that may cause low flow.
Cascade Member cannot Start Low Flow

A Cascade Member was not started due to low flow. Starting an additional member will lower the flow in the running boilers below the allowed amount.
1) Increase the flow in the system.
2) Check for restrictions that may cause low flow.
High Back Pressure in Stack or High Condensate Level

The High Back Pressure Switch and or the Condensate High Level have tripped indicating excessive Flue Back Pressure or a High Condensate Level.
1) Check for obstructions in the flue pipe.
2) Check for blocked condensate drain.
3) Check for a blocked heat exchanger.
4) Check for a blocked/ dirty burner.
5 ) Check Operation of the High Back Pressure Switch.
6) Check Operation of the Blocked Condensate Level Sensor
7) Replace the High Back Pressure Switch.
8) Replace the Bocked Condensate Sensor

1) Power the module off and on to reboot the control.
2) If the problem persists
a. Export support files from Nuro to a USB flash drive.
b. Contact Weil-McLain service, they will require these support files.

10220Waiting for BMS Header TemperatureThe BMS Header Temperature has not been sent or the BMS Heartbeat has not been updated in the BMS Heartbeat Timeout Period
1) Check to make sure the Boiler is still communicating to the BMS System
2) If the boiler is not getting the Header Temperature from the BMS System then change the Header Temperature Source

10221BMS Header Temperature out-of-rangeThe BMS Header Temperature is out-of-range
The valid temperatures are between
-40 degrees C and 130 degrees C

10222Waiting for Outdoor Air TemperatureThe BMS Outdoor Air Temperature has not been sent or the BMS Heartbeat has not been updated in the BMS Heartbeat Timeout Period
1) Check to make sure the Boiler is still communicating to the BMS System
2) If the boiler is not getting the Outdoor Air Temperature from the BMS System then change the Outdoor Air Temperature Source

10223BMS Outdoor Air Temperature out-of rangeThe BMS Outdoor Temperature is out-of-range
The valid temperatures are between
-40 degrees C and 130 degrees C

10224Waiting for Wireless Outdoor Air TemperatureThe Wireless Outdoor Air Temperature has not been sent to the boiler
1) Check to make sure the Wireless Outdoor Air Sensor is paired with the controller
2) Check to make sure the Wireless Outdoor Air Sensor has working batteries
3) Check to make sure the Wireless Outdoor Air Sensor is within the wireless transmit range
4) If the boiler is not getting the Outdoor Air Temperature from a wireless Outdoor Air source then change the Outdoor Air Temperature Source

10225Wireless Outdoor Air Temperature out-of-rangeThe Wireless Outdoor Air Temperatue is not reporting a valid Outdoor Air Temperature
1) Check to make sure the Wireless Outdoor Air Sensor has working batteries
2) Check to make sure the Wireless Outdoor Air Sensor is within the wireless transmit range

10226Waiting for BMS Analog Input ValueThe BMS Analog Input has not been sent or the BMS Heartbeat has not been updated in the BMS Heartbeat Timeout Period
1) Check to make sure the Boiler is still communicating to the BMS System
2) If the boiler is not getting the Analog Input from the BMS System then change the Firing Rate Source

10227BMS Analog Input out-of-rangeThe BMS Analog Input is out-of-range
The valid range are numbers between
40 and 200 which relates to .1mA precession

10228BMS Heartbeat LostThe BMS Heartbeat has not been updated in the BMS Heartbeat Timeout Period
1) Check to make sure the Appliance is still in communication with the BMS System
2) Should the Appliance be using a BMS Heartbeat? if not change the BMS Heartbeat parameter

10229DHW Temperature Source InvalidThe DHW Temperature Source is Invaild for the DHW Control Method
1) The Appliance will use its DHW sensor and is capable of running in DHW Mode if its sensor is shorted
2) This error is from the DHW Temperature Source being set to BMS DHW Temperature when in DHW Control Method Thermostat
3) Change the DHW Temperature Source or DHW Control Method

10230Waiting for BMS DHW TemperatureThe BMS DHW Temperature has not been sent or the BMS Heartbeat has not been updated in the BMS Heartbeat Timeout Period
1) Check to make sure the Appliance is still communicating to the BMS System
2) If the Appliance is not getting the DHW Temperature from the BMS System then change the DHW Temperature Source

10231BMS DHW Temperature out-of-rangeThe BMS DHW Temperature is out-of-range
The valid temperatures are between
-40 degrees C and 130 degrees C

10232The Appliance Model is unknownThe Appliance Model is unknown.
The Appliance Model needs to be defined before theAppliance can operate.
If this is a new NURO controller please follow the procedure to select the Appliance Model

10233Unknown SOLA VersionThe SOLA that is connected is not the a known version that can work with the NURO control
1) Try cycling power
2) Check the communication between the NURO and the SOLA
3) Contact the factory for a replacement SOLA

10234Unknown SOLA PasswordThe SOLA's password is unknown
1) Try cycling power
2) Check the communication between the NURO and the SOLA
3) Contact the factory for a replacement SOLA

10235High Gas Limit / Dual Fuel RelaysThe high gas limit switch has tripped or the Dual Fuel Circuit has detected a problem
1. Check for proper gas valve adjustment.
2. Check for proper gas valve operation.
3. Check fire test valve.
4. Check for proper wiring.
5.Replace switch.
-----------------------------------
1) Check to make sure both Gas Valves do not open simultaneously when the boiler atempts to start.
2) Verify only one Current Switch relay is active at a time when the boiler atempts to start

10236High Back Pressure in Stack or Burner HoodOne or more High Back Pressure Switches has tripped indicating excessive Flue Back Pressure or High Pressure in the Burner.
1) Check for obstructions in the flue pipe.
2) Check for blocked condensate drain.
3) Check for a blocked heat exchanger.
4) Check for a blocked/ dirty burner.
5 ) Check Operation of the High Back Pressure Switches.
4) Replace the High Back Pressure Switches.
10237Alternate Header Sensor Being UsedThe primary selected Header Sensor failed. Check the sensor.

10238Stack sensor fault1. Check wiring and correct any possible errors.
2. Check the Stack Limit Switch. If tripped perform a-d and reset the switch

a.Check for fouled heat exchanger.
b.Check for proper combustion
c.check for proper fan speed
d.Check for proper settings

3. Replace the Stack sensor or Stack Limit Switch.
4. If previous steps are correct and fault persists,
a. Export support files from Nuro to a USB flash drive.
b. Contact Weil-McLain service, they will require these support files..

10239Burner Door or HX High Temp FaultThe burner door switch or the heat exchanger switch has tripped indicating excessive temperature on the burner door or rear heat exchanger.
1. Determine which switch is tripped.
If either switch is tripped: contact Patterson Kelley factory support.
2.If neither switch is tripped, check the wiring and correct any errors.
3. If previous steps are correct and the fault persists,
a. Export support files from Nuro to a USB flash drive.
b. Contact Weil-McLain service, they will require these support files..

10240Low Water LimitThe external Low water level device has tripped indicating insufficient water level in the boiler, or the external jumper is missing

1. Check the external Low Water Sensor (if used) or the terminal strip jumper.
2. Check boiler pump for proper operation.
3. Check the external low water level switch.
4. Check the external low water level probe and connections.

10241Flow Switch opened during runThe flow switch opened when it should have been closed.
1. Check the pump
2. Check for flow obstructions

10242Lightoff Rate Proving RecycleThe Fan Speed was not steady during Ignition.
1. Check fan wiring and correct any potential wiring errors.
2. Check that the fan indicates proper RPM.
3. Check ignitor gap.
4. Check proper electrical grounding.

10243Outdated Member SoftwareOne or All of the Members have Outdated Software. In order to run the Delta T Monitoring the Member software needs to be updated. Please update all the Members to the latest software version.

10244Air Inlet Sensor FaultThe Air Inlet Sensor is faulted.
This sensor is connected to the Spare Sensor Input.
The parameter set is configured to use the Spare Sensor as an Air Inlet temperature sensor
1. Check the spare sensor.
2. Check wiring to the spare sensor.
3. Check that parameters are set correctly if no sensor is wired to the spare sensor terminals.

10245ODA Sensor FaultThe ODA Sensor is faulted.
The parameter set is configured to use the ODA sensor for freeze protection.
1. Check the outdoor air sensor.
2. Check wiring to the outdoor air sensor.
3. Check that parameters are set correctly.

10246Low Air Intake Prssure LimitThe Low Air Intake Pressure Switch has tripped indicating excessive negative inlet pressure.
1) Check for obstructions in the air inlet pipe.
2) Check for blocked air inlet
3 ) Check operation of the Low Air Inlet Pressure Switch.
4) Replace the Low Air Inlet Pressure Switch.

10247Cascade Member Shutdown Low FlowA Cascade Member was shutdown due to low flow. The Delta T was higher than allowed.
1) Increase the flow in the system.
2) Check for restrictions that may cause low flow.

10248Cascade Member cannot Start Low FlowA Cascade Member was not started due to low flow. Starting an additional member will lower the flow in the running boilers below the allowed amount.
1) Increase the flow in the system.
2) Check for restrictions that may cause low flow.

10249High Back Pressure in Stack or High Condensate LevelThe High Back Pressure Switch and or the Condensate High Level have tripped indicating excessive Flue Back Pressure or a High Condensate Level.
1) Check for obstructions in the flue pipe.
2) Check for blocked condensate drain.
3) Check for a blocked heat exchanger.
4) Check for a blocked/ dirty burner.
5 ) Check Operation of the High Back Pressure Switch.
6) Check Operation of the Blocked Condensate Level Sensor
7) Replace the High Back Pressure Switch.
8) Replace the Bocked Condensate Sensor
